501	    def _create_run(self, run, plan):
502	        """Append creation events and persist a freshly built run.
503	
504	        A run with a future ``not_before`` stays fully ``pending``: its root
505	        nodes are opened (one ``ready``/``waiting`` history event each) only
506	        when the first claim arrives at or after that time.  A past, present
507	        or missing start time opens the roots immediately, exactly like the
508	        legacy create behavior.
509	        """
510	        run_id = run["run_id"]
511	        self._event(run, run_id, None, "run_created")
512	        not_before = run.get("not_before")
513	        if not_before is None or float(not_before) <= self.now():
514	            self._open_root_nodes(run)
515	        run["status"], run["updated_at"] = _derive_run_status(run), self._iso()
516	        return self.store.save_run(run)

518	    def _open_root_nodes(self, run, when=None):
519	        """Settle every pending node whose dependencies are decided.
520	
521	        Each unlocked or skipped node records exactly one ``ready``,
522	        ``waiting`` or ``skipped`` history event, emitted in topological
523	        order, so calling this on repeated claims never re-opens a node.
524	        Returns the ``(step_id, new_status)`` transitions.
525	        """
526	        now_iso = self._iso() if when is None else when
527	        opened = _promote_pending(run, now_iso)
528	        for sid, status in opened:
529	            attempt = 0 if status == STEP_WAITING else run["steps"][sid]["attempt"]
530	            self._event(run, run["run_id"], sid, status, attempt=attempt)
531	        return opened

598	    def list_audit(self, tenant, action=None, run_id=None, limit=100, after=0):
599	        """Read the tenant's audit stream; never mutates any state.
600	
601	        Returns ``(items, next_after)`` where ``items`` are the tenant's
602	        audit records with ``sequence > after`` (optionally filtered by
603	        ``action`` and/or ``run_id``) in ascending sequence order, at most
604	        ``limit`` of them, and ``next_after`` is the sequence of the last
605	        record of the page, or ``None`` when no further records follow.
606	        Only the requesting tenant's own stream is ever read.
607	        """
608	        tenant = normalize_tenant(tenant)
609	        if action is not None:
610	            if not isinstance(action, str) or not action.strip():
611	                raise WorkflowError("action must be a non-empty string", "bad_action")
612	            action = action.strip()
613	        if run_id is not None:
614	            if not isinstance(run_id, str) or not run_id.strip():
615	                raise WorkflowError("run_id must be a non-empty string", "bad_run_id")
616	            run_id = run_id.strip()
617	        if isinstance(limit, bool) or not isinstance(limit, int) or not 1 <= limit <= 1000:
618	            raise WorkflowError("limit must be an integer between 1 and 1000", "bad_limit")
619	        if isinstance(after, bool) or not isinstance(after, int) or after < 0:
620	            raise WorkflowError("after must be a non-negative integer", "bad_after")
621	        with self.store.locked():
622	            matched = [r for r in self.store.load_audit(tenant) if r["sequence"] > after]
623	        if action is not None:
624	            matched = [r for r in matched if r["action"] == action]
625	        if run_id is not None:
626	            matched = [r for r in matched if r.get("run_id") == run_id]
627	        matched.sort(key=lambda r: r["sequence"])
628	        page = matched[:limit]
629	        next_after = page[-1]["sequence"] if len(matched) > limit else None
630	        return page, next_after

855	        reclaimed = []

869	    def claim(self, tenant, run_id, worker_id, lease_seconds=30):
870	        """Lease the next ready step, or return ``None`` when none is ready.
871	
872	        A delayed run (a future ``not_before``) cannot be activated early:
873	        claims before the start time return ``None`` without touching its
874	        state, history or ``updated_at``.  The first claim at or after the
875	        start time opens the root nodes (one ``ready``/``waiting`` event each)
876	        and then leases at most one task under the usual order and quota; a
877	        run whose roots are all approvals activates and still returns ``None``.
878	
879	        Once the tenant has any registered worker the claim must come from an
880	        active registration (``worker_not_registered`` / ``worker_expired``);
881	        a tenant with no registrations keeps the legacy non-empty-id rule.
882	
883	        A ready step whose retry backoff is still pending
884	        (``next_attempt_at`` in the future) is not leased; other ready tasks
885	        whose backoff has elapsed are handed out in the usual order instead.
886	        When nothing is leased and no lease takeover or root activation
887	        happened, the run's state, history and ``updated_at`` are left
888	        exactly as stored.
889	
890	        When the tenant has a concurrency quota configured (see
891	        :meth:`set_quota`), all of the tenant's runs share one active-lease
892	        budget: expired leases across every run are reclaimed first (with
893	        the usual ``takeover`` events, kept even when the budget turns out
894	        full), and a full budget returns ``None`` without a claim event.
895	        Tenants without a configured quota keep the legacy behavior exactly.
896	        """
897	        if not isinstance(worker_id, str) or not worker_id.strip():
898	            raise WorkflowError("worker_id must be a non-empty string", "bad_worker")
899	        if not isinstance(lease_seconds, (int, float)) or isinstance(lease_seconds, bool) \
900	                or lease_seconds <= 0:
901	            raise WorkflowError("lease_seconds must be a positive number", "bad_lease")
902	        now = self.now()
903	        with self.store.locked():
904	            owner = self.store.run_exists(run_id)
905	            if owner is not None and owner != tenant:
906	                raise WorkflowError("run %s belongs to another tenant" % run_id, "cross_tenant")
907	            # Once a tenant has any registered worker, claims require an
908	            # active registration; a tenant without records keeps the legacy
909	            # "any non-empty worker_id" rule.
910	            self._check_worker_registration(tenant, worker_id.strip(), now)
911	            run = self.get_run(tenant, run_id)
912	            not_before = run.get("not_before")
913	            if not_before is not None and float(not_before) > now:
914	                # Still sleeping: activation happens only via a due claim.
915	                return None
916	            if run["status"] == RUN_PAUSED:
917	                # Frozen by the tenant: no activation, reclaim or lease.
918	                return None
919	            tenant_quota = self._tenant_quota_limit(tenant)
920	            if tenant_quota is None:
921	                reclaimed = self._expire_leases(run, now)
922	            else:
923	                # A configured tenant quota shares one lease budget across
924	                # all of the tenant's runs: reclaim every expired lease of
925	                # the tenant under this lock, then count what survives.
926	                others = [r for r in self.store.load_all_runs(tenant)
927	                          if r["run_id"] != run_id]
928	                self._reclaim_tenant_leases(others, now)
929	                reclaimed = self._expire_leases(run, now)
930	                active = _active_lease_count(run, now) + sum(
931	                    _active_lease_count(other, now) for other in others)
932	                if active >= tenant_quota:
933	                    # Budget exhausted: this call's takeovers are kept, but
934	                    # no claim event and no other state change is added.
935	                    if reclaimed:
936	                        run["status"] = _derive_run_status(run)
937	                        run["updated_at"] = self._iso()
938	                        self.store.save_run(run)
939	                    return None
940	            opened = self._open_root_nodes(run)
941	            now_iso = self._iso()
942	            candidates = [s for s in run["steps"].values()
943	                          if s["status"] == STEP_READY and _retry_due(s, now_iso)]
944	            index = run["order_index"]
945	            quota = run.get("max_parallelism")
946	            at_quota = quota is not None and _active_lease_count(run, now) >= int(quota)
947	            step = (min(candidates, key=lambda s: (index.get(s["id"], 0), s["id"]))
948	                    if candidates and not at_quota else None)
949	            previous = run["status"]
950	            if step is not None:
951	                step.update(status=STEP_RUNNING, worker_id=worker_id, next_attempt_at=None,
952	                            lease_deadline=now + float(lease_seconds), started_at=self._iso())
953	                self._event(run, run_id, step["id"], "claim", attempt=step["attempt"],
954	                            worker_id=worker_id, lease_deadline=step["lease_deadline"])
955	            elif not reclaimed and not opened:
956	                # Nothing to lease and nothing else changed: keep the stored
957	                # state, history and updated_at untouched.
958	                return None
959	            run["status"] = _derive_run_status(run)
960	            if step is not None and run["status"] == RUN_RUNNING and previous == RUN_PENDING:
961	                self._event(run, run_id, None, "run_started")
962	            run["updated_at"] = self._iso()
963	            self.store.save_run(run)
964	            return dict(step) if step is not None else None

966	    def claim_fair(self, tenant, worker_id, lease_seconds=30):
967	        """Lease one task from the tenant's least-claimed eligible run.
968	
969	        Scans every run of the tenant.  First, sleeping runs whose
970	        ``not_before`` has come due are activated (root nodes opened, one
971	        ``ready``/``waiting`` event each) in ``run_id`` order.  Then the
972	        candidates — runs that are not terminal, not still sleeping, hold at
973	        least one ``ready`` ordinary task whose retry backoff has elapsed
974	        (``next_attempt_at`` reached) and have not reached their
975	        ``max_parallelism`` — are ordered by fairness: the number of
976	        ``claim`` events in the run's history (fewest first), then
977	        ``created_at``, then ``run_id``.  A run holding only not-yet-due
978	        retries is skipped and its fairness count is left alone.  Expired
979	        leases are reclaimed with the usual ``takeover`` events before slots
980	        are counted, exactly like the single-run claim.  The winner leases
981	        its next due task in ``(topological index, step id)`` order,
982	        recording the usual ``claim`` and, when the run leaves ``pending``,
983	        ``run_started`` events.
984	
985	        Returns ``(run_id, step)`` or ``None`` when no run is eligible; at
986	        most one task is leased per call.  The fairness count is rebuilt
987	        from the append-only history on every call, so restarts, replay and
988	        concurrent callers (serialized by the store lock) all agree.
989	        Worker-registration gating matches the single-run claim.
990	
991	        A configured tenant concurrency quota (see :meth:`set_quota`) adds a
992	        shared active-lease budget across all of the tenant's runs: expired
993	        leases tenant-wide are reclaimed first (takeovers are kept), and a
994	        full budget returns ``None`` before any run is activated or leased.
995	        """
996	        tenant = normalize_tenant(tenant)
997	        worker_id = normalize_worker_id(worker_id)
998	        lease = normalize_worker_lease(lease_seconds)
999	        now = self.now()
1000	        with self.store.locked():
1001	            self._check_worker_registration(tenant, worker_id, now)
1002	            runs = self.store.load_all_runs(tenant)
1003	            tenant_quota = self._tenant_quota_limit(tenant)
1004	            if tenant_quota is not None:
1005	                # Shared tenant budget: reclaim every expired lease of the
1006	                # tenant under this lock, then count the surviving active
1007	                # leases.  A full budget returns nothing; the takeovers
1008	                # recorded by the reclaim are kept.
1009	                self._reclaim_tenant_leases(runs, now)
1010	                if sum(_active_lease_count(run, now) for run in runs) >= tenant_quota:
1011	                    return None
1012	            # Activate due sleeping runs in run_id order; already-activated
1013	            # runs are left untouched.  Terminal runs (including a cancelled
1014	            # run whose roots were never opened) and paused runs are never
1015	            # activated.
1016	            for run in runs:
1017	                if run["status"] in TERMINAL_RUN_STATES or run["status"] == RUN_PAUSED:
1018	                    continue
1019	                not_before = run.get("not_before")
1020	                if not_before is None or float(not_before) > now:
1021	                    continue
1022	                if _roots_opened(run):
1023	                    continue
1024	                self._open_root_nodes(run)
1025	                run["status"] = _derive_run_status(run)
1026	                run["updated_at"] = self._iso()
1027	                self.store.save_run(run)
1028	            # Pick the fairest eligible run.
1029	            now_iso = self._iso(now)
1030	            best_key, best_run, best_previous = None, None, None
1031	            for run in runs:
1032	                if run["status"] in TERMINAL_RUN_STATES or run["status"] == RUN_PAUSED:
1033	                    continue
1034	                not_before = run.get("not_before")
1035	                if not_before is not None and float(not_before) > now:
1036	                    continue
1037	                previous = run["status"]
1038	                reclaimed = self._expire_leases(run, now)
1039	                if reclaimed:
1040	                    run["status"] = _derive_run_status(run)
1041	                    run["updated_at"] = self._iso()
1042	                    self.store.save_run(run)
1043	                ready = [s for s in run["steps"].values()
1044	                         if s["status"] == STEP_READY and _retry_due(s, now_iso)]
1045	                if not ready:
1046	                    continue
1047	                quota = run.get("max_parallelism")
1048	                if quota is not None and _active_lease_count(run, now) >= int(quota):
1049	                    continue
1050	                claims = sum(1 for e in run["history"] if e.get("type") == "claim")
1051	                key = (claims, run.get("created_at") or "", run["run_id"])
1052	                if best_key is None or key < best_key:
1053	                    best_key, best_run, best_previous = key, run, previous
1054	            if best_run is None:
1055	                return None
1056	            run = best_run
1057	            index = run["order_index"]
1058	            step = min((s for s in run["steps"].values()
1059	                        if s["status"] == STEP_READY and _retry_due(s, now_iso)),
1060	                       key=lambda s: (index.get(s["id"], 0), s["id"]))
1061	            step.update(status=STEP_RUNNING, worker_id=worker_id, next_attempt_at=None,
1062	                        lease_deadline=now + lease, started_at=self._iso())
1063	            self._event(run, run["run_id"], step["id"], "claim", attempt=step["attempt"],
1064	                        worker_id=worker_id, lease_deadline=step["lease_deadline"])
1065	            run["status"] = _derive_run_status(run)
1066	            if run["status"] == RUN_RUNNING and best_previous == RUN_PENDING:
1067	                self._event(run, run["run_id"], None, "run_started")
1068	            run["updated_at"] = self._iso()
1069	            self.store.save_run(run)
1070	            return run["run_id"], dict(step)

1220	        binding or its history.  A run that is already ``succeeded`` or
1221	        ``failed`` conflicts (``run_finished``); a run that is already

1235	            if owner != tenant:
1236	                raise WorkflowError("run %s belongs to another tenant" % run_id, "cross_tenant")

1240	                return run
1241	            if run["status"] in (RUN_SUCCEEDED, RUN_FAILED):
1242	                raise ConflictError("run %s is already %s" % (run_id, run["status"]),
1243	                                    "run_finished")
1244	            index = run["order_index"]
1245	            for sid in sorted(run["steps"], key=lambda s: index.get(s, 0)):
1246	                step = run["steps"][sid]
1247	                if step["status"] in TERMINAL_STEP_STATES:
1248	                    continue
1249	                holder = step.get("worker_id")
1250	                step.update(status=STEP_CANCELLED, worker_id=None, lease_deadline=None,
1251	                            next_attempt_at=None)
1252	                self._event(run, run_id, sid, "cancel", attempt=step["attempt"],
1253	                            worker_id=holder, actor=actor)
1254	            run["status"] = RUN_CANCELLED
1255	            self._event(run, run_id, None, "run_cancelled", actor=actor)
1256	            run["updated_at"] = self._iso()
1257	            self.store.save_run(run)
1258	            return run
1259	
1260	    # -- pause / resume ------------------------------------------------
1261	    @staticmethod
1262	    def _normalize_actor(actor):
1263	        if not isinstance(actor, str):
1264	            raise WorkflowError("actor must be a string", "bad_actor")
1265	        actor = actor.strip()
1266	        if not actor:
1267	            raise WorkflowError("actor must be a non-empty string", "bad_actor")
1268	        return actor
1269	
1270	    def pause(self, tenant, run_id, actor):
1271	        """Freeze an unfinished run; a repeat pause is a no-op.
1272	
1273	        Only a ``pending`` or ``running`` run can be paused.  Every
1274	        ``running`` task releases its lease and goes back to ``ready`` with
1275	        ``worker_id``, ``lease_deadline`` and ``next_attempt_at`` cleared and
1276	        its ``attempt`` unchanged, recording one ``pause`` event per revoked
1277	        task in topological order; a final run-level ``run_paused`` event
1278	        carrying the actor closes the transition, and the audit stream
1279	        follows the same order.  Completed nodes, waiting approvals and a
1280	        not-yet-due delayed start are preserved exactly: no node is opened,
1281	        no attempt is counted and ``not_before`` is untouched.  Freed leases
1282	        stop counting against the tenant quota immediately, so ``complete``,
1283	        ``fail`` and ``heartbeat`` against the revoked tasks all fail, and
1284	        claims hand out nothing while the run is paused.
1285	
1286	        A run that is already ``paused`` returns the current document
1287	        without new history, audit records or a changed ``updated_at``; a
1288	        ``succeeded``, ``failed`` or ``cancelled`` run conflicts
1289	        (``run_finished``).
1290	        """
1291	        tenant = normalize_tenant(tenant)
1292	        actor = self._normalize_actor(actor)
1293	        with self.store.locked():
1294	            owner = self.store.run_exists(run_id)
1295	            if owner is None:
1296	                raise WorkflowError("unknown run: %s" % run_id, "unknown_run")
1297	            if owner != tenant:
1298	                raise WorkflowError("run %s belongs to another tenant" % run_id, "cross_tenant")
1299	            run = self.get_run(tenant, run_id)
1300	            if run["status"] == RUN_PAUSED:
1301	                # Idempotent repeat: the stored document is returned as is.
1302	                return run
1303	            if run["status"] in TERMINAL_RUN_STATES:
1304	                raise ConflictError("run %s is already %s" % (run_id, run["status"]),
1305	                                    "run_finished")
1306	            index = run["order_index"]
1307	            for sid in sorted(run["steps"], key=lambda s: index.get(s, 0)):
1308	                step = run["steps"][sid]
1309	                if step["status"] != STEP_RUNNING:
1310	                    continue
1311	                holder = step.get("worker_id")
1312	                step.update(status=STEP_READY, worker_id=None, lease_deadline=None,
1313	                            next_attempt_at=None)
1314	                self._event(run, run_id, sid, "pause", attempt=step["attempt"],
1315	                            worker_id=holder, actor=actor)
1316	            run["status"] = RUN_PAUSED
1317	            self._event(run, run_id, None, "run_paused", actor=actor)
1318	            run["updated_at"] = self._iso()
1319	            self.store.save_run(run)
1320	            return run
1321	
1322	    def resume(self, tenant, run_id, actor):
1323	        """Unfreeze a paused run; a repeat resume is a no-op.
1324	
1325	        Only a ``paused`` run can be resumed.  The run goes back to the
1326	        status its nodes derive (``pending`` or ``running``) and a run-level
1327	        ``run_resumed`` event carrying the actor is appended; no task is
1328	        leased, no node is opened and a not-yet-due ``not_before`` still
1329	        gates activation, so work continues only through later claims.  Any
1330	        other state conflicts (``not_paused``) — except the idempotent
1331	        repeat of a resume that already happened, which returns the current
1332	        document without new history, audit records or a changed
1333	        ``updated_at``.
1334	        """
1335	        tenant = normalize_tenant(tenant)
1336	        actor = self._normalize_actor(actor)
1337	        with self.store.locked():
1338	            owner = self.store.run_exists(run_id)
1339	            if owner is None:
1340	                raise WorkflowError("unknown run: %s" % run_id, "unknown_run")
1341	            if owner != tenant:
1342	                raise WorkflowError("run %s belongs to another tenant" % run_id, "cross_tenant")
1343	            run = self.get_run(tenant, run_id)
1344	            if run["status"] == RUN_PAUSED:
1345	                run["status"] = _derive_run_status(run)
1346	                self._event(run, run_id, None, "run_resumed", actor=actor)
1347	                run["updated_at"] = self._iso()
1348	                self.store.save_run(run)
1349	                return run
1350	            if run["status"] not in TERMINAL_RUN_STATES:
1351	                markers = [e.get("type") for e in run["history"]
1352	                           if e.get("type") in ("run_paused", "run_resumed")]
1353	                if markers and markers[-1] == "run_resumed":
1354	                    # Idempotent repeat: the stored document is returned as is.
1355	                    return run
1356	            raise ConflictError("run %s is not paused" % run_id, "not_paused")
1357	
1358	    # -- human decisions -----------------------------------------------
1359	    def decide(self, tenant, run_id, step_id, actor, decision):
1360	        """Record a human approve/reject decision for an approval step.
1361	
1362	        Repeating the *same* decision from the *same* actor is idempotent and
1363	        returns the unchanged run; a different actor or the opposite decision
1364	        conflicts with the recorded decision.
1365	        """
1366	        if not isinstance(actor, str) or not actor.strip():
1367	            raise WorkflowError("actor must be a non-empty string", "bad_actor")
1368	        actor = actor.strip()
1369	        if decision not in ("approve", "reject"):
1370	            raise WorkflowError("decision must be 'approve' or 'reject'", "bad_decision")
1371	        with self.store.locked():
1372	            run = self.get_run(tenant, run_id)
1373	            if run["status"] == RUN_CANCELLED:
1374	                raise ConflictError("run %s is cancelled" % run_id, "run_cancelled")
1375	            if run["status"] == RUN_PAUSED:
1376	                raise ConflictError("run %s is paused" % run_id, "run_paused")
1377	            step = run["steps"].get(step_id)
1378	            if step is None:
1379	                raise WorkflowError("unknown step: %s" % step_id, "unknown_step")
1380	            if step.get("kind") != KIND_APPROVAL:
1381	                raise ConflictError("step %s is not an approval node" % step_id, "not_an_approval")
1382	            recorded = step.get("approval")
1383	            if recorded is not None:
1384	                if recorded["actor"] == actor and recorded["decision"] == decision:
1385	                    return run
1386	                raise ConflictError(
1387	                    "step %s already decided by %s: %s"
1388	                    % (step_id, recorded["actor"], recorded["decision"]),
1389	                    "already_decided",
1390	                )
1391	            if step["status"] != STEP_WAITING:
1392	                raise ConflictError(
1393	                    "step %s is not waiting for a decision" % step_id, "not_waiting"
1394	                )
1395	            event = self._event(run, run_id, step_id, "decision", attempt=0, worker_id=None,
1396	                                actor=actor, decision=decision)
1397	            at = event["at"]
1398	            step["approval"] = {"actor": actor, "decision": decision, "at": at}
1399	            previous = run["status"]
1400	            if decision == "approve":
1401	                step.update(status=STEP_SUCCEEDED, finished_at=at)
1402	            else:
1403	                step.update(status=STEP_FAILED, finished_at=at)
1404	            # Either way the node is terminal now: dependents governed by
1405	            # custom trigger rules may unlock or skip.  All-all_success runs
1406	            # derive the same immediate failure as before on a reject.
1407	            self._open_root_nodes(run, at)
1408	            run["status"] = _derive_run_status(run)
1409	            if run["status"] == RUN_RUNNING and previous == RUN_PENDING:
1410	                self._event(run, run_id, None, "run_started")
1411	            if run["status"] == RUN_SUCCEEDED:
1412	                self._event(run, run_id, None, "run_succeeded")
1413	            elif run["status"] == RUN_FAILED:
1414	                self._event(run, run_id, None, "run_failed")
1415	            run["updated_at"] = at
1416	            self.store.save_run(run)
1417	            return run
1418	
1419	    # -- history / replay ----------------------------------------------
1420	    def replay(self, tenant, run_id):
1421	        """Rebuild run state from the run's frozen definition and history.
1422	
1423	        Nodes are rebuilt from the normalized DAG snapshotted into the run
1424	        document at creation time, never from the workflow currently stored
1425	        under the run's ``workflow_id``: a later same-name submission may
1426	        replace that workflow, but existing runs keep their original step
1427	        order, node kinds, dependencies, ``max_attempts`` and state-machine
1428	        semantics.  Documents written before snapshots existed reconstruct
1429	        the plan from the definitions and order saved in the run itself.
1430	
1431	        The result agrees with the persisted run on every observable field —
1432	        ``run_id``, ``workflow_id``, ``step_order``, run and per-step
1433	        ``status``, ``attempt``, ``worker_id``, ``lease_deadline``,
1434	        ``next_attempt_at``, ``ready_at``, ``started_at``, ``finished_at``,
1435	        ``result``, ``error`` and ``approval`` — and the append-only history
1436	        is the sole source of transitions, so replaying again, including
1437	        after a restart, yields the identical document.
1438	        """
1439	        owner = self.store.run_exists(run_id)
1440	        if owner is None:
1441	            raise WorkflowError("unknown run: %s" % run_id, "unknown_run")
1442	        if owner != tenant:
1443	            raise WorkflowError("run %s belongs to another tenant" % run_id, "cross_tenant")
1444	        stored = self.store.load_run(tenant, run_id)
1445	        plan = run_plan(stored)
1446	        rebuilt = new_run(tenant, stored["workflow_id"], run_id, stored.get("params"), plan,
1447	                          stored["created_at"],
1448	                          max_parallelism=stored.get("max_parallelism"),
1449	                          idempotency_key=stored.get("idempotency_key"),
1450	                          not_before=stored.get("not_before"),
1451	                          schedule_id=stored.get("schedule_id"),
1452	                          scheduled_at=stored.get("scheduled_at"))
1453	        # The fresh document must carry exactly the frozen snapshot and
1454	        # ordering of the stored run (new_run fills them from the same plan
1455	        # already, but align them defensively for reconstructed old plans).
1456	        rebuilt["plan"] = copy.deepcopy(plan)
1457	        rebuilt["step_order"] = list(plan["order"])
1458	        rebuilt["order_index"] = {sid: i for i, sid in enumerate(plan["order"])}
1459	        steps = rebuilt["steps"]
1460	        paused = False
1461	        for event in stored["history"]:
1462	            sid, etype, at = event.get("step_id"), event.get("type"), event.get("at")
1463	            attempt = event.get("attempt")
1464	            if sid is None:
1465	                # Run-level markers (run_created, run_started, run_succeeded,
1466	                # run_failed, run_cancelled) need no replay action: the run
1467	                # status is derived from the rebuilt nodes at the end,
1468	                # exactly as every live transition derives it before
1469	                # persisting.  run_paused/run_resumed only toggle whether
1470	                # that derived status is reported as paused.
1471	                if etype == "run_paused":
1472	                    paused = True
1473	                elif etype == "run_resumed":
1474	                    paused = False
1475	                continue
1476	            step = steps.get(sid)
1477	            if step is None:
1478	                # The frozen definition has no node for this event: a node
1479	                # introduced by a later same-name workflow must not appear
1480	                # here, and old events can never reference a removed node.
1481	                continue
1482	            if etype == "ready":
1483	                step.update(status=STEP_READY, ready_at=at)
1484	            elif etype == "waiting":
1485	                step.update(status=STEP_WAITING)
1486	            elif etype == "skipped":
1487	                # Mirrors the settle pass: the node never ran, keeps its
1488	                # attempt and holds no lease fields.
1489	                step.update(status=STEP_SKIPPED)
1490	            elif etype == "claim":
1491	                step.update(status=STEP_RUNNING, worker_id=event.get("worker_id"),
1492	                            started_at=at, lease_deadline=event.get("lease_deadline"),
1493	                            next_attempt_at=None)
1494	            elif etype == "heartbeat":
1495	                step["lease_deadline"] = event.get("lease_deadline")
1496	            elif etype == "takeover":
1497	                # Mirrors _expire_leases: the node is re-queued with a fresh
1498	                # ready_at and no holder; started_at from the lost lease is
1499	                # left in place, exactly as the live transition leaves it.
1500	                step.update(status=STEP_READY, worker_id=None, lease_deadline=None,
1501	                            ready_at=at)
1502	            elif etype == "complete":
1503	                # Mirrors complete(): the successful node keeps the worker
1504	                # that completed it and clears any prior failure error.
1505	                step.update(status=STEP_SUCCEEDED, result=event.get("result"), error=None,
1506	                            finished_at=at, lease_deadline=None,
1507	                            worker_id=event.get("worker_id"),
1508	                            attempt=step["attempt"] if attempt is None else attempt)
1509	            elif etype == "decision":
1510	                approved = event.get("decision") == "approve"
1511	                step.update(status=STEP_SUCCEEDED if approved else STEP_FAILED,
1512	                            finished_at=at,
1513	                            approval={"actor": event.get("actor"),
1514	                                      "decision": event.get("decision"), "at": at})
1515	            elif etype == "fail":
1516	                step.update(error=event.get("error"), worker_id=None, lease_deadline=None,
1517	                            attempt=step["attempt"] if attempt is None else attempt)
1518	            elif etype == "retry":
1519	                step.update(status=STEP_READY, ready_at=at,
1520	                            next_attempt_at=event.get("next_attempt_at"))
1521	            elif etype == "attempts_exhausted":
1522	                step.update(status=STEP_FAILED, finished_at=at, next_attempt_at=None)
1523	            elif etype == "cancel":
1524	                # Mirrors cancel(): the node keeps attempt/result/error and
1525	                # releases its lease; ready_at/started_at stay as recorded.
1526	                step.update(status=STEP_CANCELLED, worker_id=None, lease_deadline=None,
1527	                            next_attempt_at=None)
1528	            elif etype == "pause":
1529	                # Mirrors pause(): the revoked task goes back to ready with
1530	                # its attempt unchanged and its lease fields cleared;
1531	                # ready_at/started_at stay as recorded.
1532	                step.update(status=STEP_READY, worker_id=None, lease_deadline=None,
1533	                            next_attempt_at=None)
1534	        # Every live write path derives the run status from its nodes, so
1535	        # rebuilding from the same nodes yields the same status — including
1536	        # the pending/running boundary (a run with only ready/waiting nodes
1537	        # and no claim is still pending; a retry-queued run has returned to
1538	        # pending even though a run_started event exists).  A pause still in
1539	        # effect reports the run as paused instead, unless a later cancel
1540	        # already moved it to a terminal state.
1541	        derived = _derive_run_status(rebuilt)
1542	        rebuilt["status"] = (RUN_PAUSED if paused and derived not in TERMINAL_RUN_STATES
1543	                             else derived)
1544	        rebuilt["updated_at"] = stored.get("updated_at")
1545	        rebuilt["history"] = copy.deepcopy(stored["history"])
1546	        return rebuilt

1	"""Persistence for flowd: workflows, runs, tenants and append-only history.
2	
3	Layout::
4	
5	    <root>/<tenant>/workflows.json
6	    <root>/<tenant>/idempotency.json
7	    <root>/<tenant>/workers.json
8	    <root>/<tenant>/schedules.json
9	    <root>/<tenant>/quota.json
10	    <root>/<tenant>/audit.json
11	    <root>/<tenant>/runs/<run_id>.json
12	
13	Every write is atomic (temp file + ``os.replace``) so a crash cannot leave a
14	half written run behind, and a fresh store over the same root sees exactly
15	the same workflows and runs.
16	"""
17	
18	import json
19	import os
20	import threading
21	import time as _time
22	import uuid
23	from contextlib import contextmanager
24	
25	from .model import KIND_TASK, TRIGGER_ALL_SUCCESS, WorkflowError, format_time, plan_workflow
26	
27	RUN_PENDING = "pending"
28	RUN_RUNNING = "running"
29	RUN_PAUSED = "paused"
30	RUN_SUCCEEDED = "succeeded"
31	RUN_FAILED = "failed"
32	RUN_CANCELLED = "cancelled"
33	
34	STEP_PENDING = "pending"
35	STEP_READY = "ready"
36	STEP_RUNNING = "running"
37	STEP_WAITING = "waiting"
38	STEP_SUCCEEDED = "succeeded"
39	STEP_FAILED = "failed"
40	STEP_CANCELLED = "cancelled"
41	STEP_SKIPPED = "skipped"
42	
43	TERMINAL_RUN_STATES = (RUN_SUCCEEDED, RUN_FAILED, RUN_CANCELLED)
44	TERMINAL_STEP_STATES = (STEP_SUCCEEDED, STEP_FAILED, STEP_CANCELLED, STEP_SKIPPED)
45	
46	
47	def atomic_write_json(path, payload):
48	    """Write ``payload`` as JSON to ``path`` atomically."""
49	    directory = os.path.dirname(path)
50	    if directory:
51	        os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
52	    tmp = "%s.tmp.%d" % (path, os.getpid())
53	    with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
54	        json.dump(payload, handle, ensure_ascii=True, sort_keys=True, indent=2)
55	        handle.flush()
56	        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
57	    os.replace(tmp, path)
58	
59	
60	def read_json(path, default=None):
61	    try:
62	        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
63	            return json.load(handle)
64	    except FileNotFoundError:
65	        return default
66	
67	
68	class WorkflowStore:
69	    """Filesystem backed store for one data directory (all tenants)."""
70	
71	    def __init__(self, root, clock=None):
72	        self.root = os.path.abspath(root)
73	        self._clock = clock if clock is not None else _time.time
74	        self._lock = threading.RLock()
75	        os.makedirs(self.root, exist_ok=True)
76	
77	    def now(self):
78	        return float(self._clock())
79	
80	    def now_iso(self):
81	        return format_time(self.now())
82	
83	    @contextmanager
84	    def locked(self):
85	        with self._lock:
86	            yield
87	
88	    # -- paths ---------------------------------------------------------
89	    def tenant_dir(self, tenant):
90	        if not isinstance(tenant, str) or not tenant.strip():
91	            raise WorkflowError("tenant must be a non-empty string", "bad_tenant")
92	        return os.path.join(self.root, tenant.strip())
93	
94	    def workflows_path(self, tenant):
95	        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "workflows.json")
96	
97	    def idempotency_path(self, tenant):
98	        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "idempotency.json")
99	
100	    def workers_path(self, tenant):
101	        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "workers.json")
102	
103	    def schedules_path(self, tenant):
104	        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "schedules.json")
105	
106	    def quota_path(self, tenant):
107	        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "quota.json")
108	
109	    def audit_path(self, tenant):
110	        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "audit.json")
111	
112	    def run_path(self, tenant, run_id):
113	        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "runs", "%s.json" % run_id)
114	
115	    def generate_run_id(self):
116	        return "run-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
117	
118	    # -- workflows -----------------------------------------------------
119	    def save_workflow(self, tenant, workflow_id, steps):
120	        plan = plan_workflow(workflow_id, steps)
121	        with self._lock:
122	            data = self.load_workflows(tenant)
123	            data[plan["workflow_id"]] = plan
124	            atomic_write_json(self.workflows_path(tenant), data)
125	        return plan
126	
127	    def load_workflows(self, tenant):
128	        return read_json(self.workflows_path(tenant), {}) or {}
129	
130	    def get_workflow(self, tenant, workflow_id):
131	        plan = self.load_workflows(tenant).get(workflow_id)
132	        if plan is None:
133	            raise WorkflowError("unknown workflow: %s" % workflow_id, "unknown_workflow")
134	        return plan
135	
136	    # -- idempotency index --------------------------------------------
137	    def load_idempotency(self, tenant):
138	        """Return the tenant's ``{trimmed key: {"run_id": ...}}`` map."""
139	        return read_json(self.idempotency_path(tenant), {}) or {}
140	
141	    def save_idempotency(self, tenant, index):
142	        atomic_write_json(self.idempotency_path(tenant), index)
143	        return index
144	
145	    # -- worker registry ----------------------------------------------
146	    def load_workers(self, tenant):
147	        """Return the tenant's ``{worker_id: registration record}`` map."""
148	        return read_json(self.workers_path(tenant), {}) or {}
149	
150	    def save_workers(self, tenant, index):
151	        atomic_write_json(self.workers_path(tenant), index)
152	        return index
153	
154	    # -- schedule registry --------------------------------------------
155	    def load_schedules(self, tenant):
156	        """Return the tenant's ``{schedule_id: schedule record}`` map."""
157	        return read_json(self.schedules_path(tenant), {}) or {}
158	
159	    def save_schedules(self, tenant, index):
160	        atomic_write_json(self.schedules_path(tenant), index)
161	        return index
162	
163	    def schedule_exists(self, schedule_id):
164	        """Return the tenant owning ``schedule_id``, or ``None``."""
165	        for tenant in sorted(os.listdir(self.root)):
166	            if schedule_id in (read_json(self.schedules_path(tenant), {}) or {}):
167	                return tenant

"""Persistence for flowd: workflows, runs, tenants and append-only history.

Layout::

    <root>/<tenant>/workflows.json
    <root>/<tenant>/idempotency.json
    <root>/<tenant>/workers.json
    <root>/<tenant>/schedules.json
    <root>/<tenant>/quota.json
    <root>/<tenant>/audit.json
    <root>/<tenant>/runs/<run_id>.json

Every write is atomic (temp file + ``os.replace``) so a crash cannot leave a
half written run behind, and a fresh store over the same root sees exactly
the same workflows and runs.
"""

import json
import os
import threading
import time as _time
import uuid
from contextlib import contextmanager

from .model import KIND_TASK, TRIGGER_ALL_SUCCESS, WorkflowError, format_time, plan_workflow

RUN_PENDING = "pending"
RUN_RUNNING = "running"
RUN_PAUSED = "paused"
RUN_SUCCEEDED = "succeeded"
RUN_FAILED = "failed"
RUN_CANCELLED = "cancelled"

STEP_PENDING = "pending"
STEP_READY = "ready"
STEP_RUNNING = "running"
STEP_WAITING = "waiting"
STEP_SUCCEEDED = "succeeded"
STEP_FAILED = "failed"
STEP_CANCELLED = "cancelled"
STEP_SKIPPED = "skipped"

TERMINAL_RUN_STATES = (RUN_SUCCEEDED, RUN_FAILED, RUN_CANCELLED)
TERMINAL_STEP_STATES = (STEP_SUCCEEDED, STEP_FAILED, STEP_CANCELLED, STEP_SKIPPED)


def atomic_write_json(path, payload):
    """Write ``payload`` as JSON to ``path`` atomically."""
    directory = os.path.dirname(path)
    if directory:
        os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = "%s.tmp.%d" % (path, os.getpid())
    with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        json.dump(payload, handle, ensure_ascii=True, sort_keys=True, indent=2)
        handle.flush()
        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
    os.replace(tmp, path)


def read_json(path, default=None):
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            return json.load(handle)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return default


class WorkflowStore:
    """Filesystem backed store for one data directory (all tenants)."""

    def __init__(self, root, clock=None):
        self.root = os.path.abspath(root)
        self._clock = clock if clock is not None else _time.time
        self._lock = threading.RLock()
        os.makedirs(self.root, exist_ok=True)

    def now(self):
        return float(self._clock())

    def now_iso(self):
        return format_time(self.now())

    @contextmanager
    def locked(self):
        with self._lock:
            yield

    # -- paths ---------------------------------------------------------
    def tenant_dir(self, tenant):
        if not isinstance(tenant, str) or not tenant.strip():
            raise WorkflowError("tenant must be a non-empty string", "bad_tenant")
        return os.path.join(self.root, tenant.strip())

    def workflows_path(self, tenant):
        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "workflows.json")

    def idempotency_path(self, tenant):
        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "idempotency.json")

    def workers_path(self, tenant):
        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "workers.json")

    def schedules_path(self, tenant):
        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "schedules.json")

    def quota_path(self, tenant):
        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "quota.json")

    def audit_path(self, tenant):
        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "audit.json")

    def run_path(self, tenant, run_id):
        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "runs", "%s.json" % run_id)

    def generate_run_id(self):
        return "run-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]

    # -- workflows -----------------------------------------------------
    def save_workflow(self, tenant, workflow_id, steps):
        plan = plan_workflow(workflow_id, steps)
        with self._lock:
            data = self.load_workflows(tenant)
            data[plan["workflow_id"]] = plan
            atomic_write_json(self.workflows_path(tenant), data)
        return plan

    def load_workflows(self, tenant):
        return read_json(self.workflows_path(tenant), {}) or {}

    def get_workflow(self, tenant, workflow_id):
        plan = self.load_workflows(tenant).get(workflow_id)
        if plan is None:
            raise WorkflowError("unknown workflow: %s" % workflow_id, "unknown_workflow")
        return plan

    # -- idempotency index --------------------------------------------
    def load_idempotency(self, tenant):
        """Return the tenant's ``{trimmed key: {"run_id": ...}}`` map."""
        return read_json(self.idempotency_path(tenant), {}) or {}

    def save_idempotency(self, tenant, index):
        atomic_write_json(self.idempotency_path(tenant), index)
        return index

    # -- worker registry ----------------------------------------------
    def load_workers(self, tenant):
        """Return the tenant's ``{worker_id: registration record}`` map."""
        return read_json(self.workers_path(tenant), {}) or {}

    def save_workers(self, tenant, index):
        atomic_write_json(self.workers_path(tenant), index)
        return index

    # -- schedule registry --------------------------------------------
    def load_schedules(self, tenant):
        """Return the tenant's ``{schedule_id: schedule record}`` map."""
        return read_json(self.schedules_path(tenant), {}) or {}

    def save_schedules(self, tenant, index):
        atomic_write_json(self.schedules_path(tenant), index)
        return index

    def schedule_exists(self, schedule_id):
        """Return the tenant owning ``schedule_id``, or ``None``."""
        for tenant in sorted(os.listdir(self.root)):
            if schedule_id in (read_json(self.schedules_path(tenant), {}) or {}):
                return tenant
        return None

    # -- tenant concurrency quota ---------------------------------------
    def load_quota(self, tenant):
        """Return the tenant's quota record, or ``None`` when unconfigured."""
        return read_json(self.quota_path(tenant), None)

    def save_quota(self, tenant, record):
        atomic_write_json(self.quota_path(tenant), record)
        return record

    # -- audit stream ---------------------------------------------------
    def append_audit(self, tenant, action, at=None, run_id=None, step_id=None,
                     workflow_id=None, schedule_id=None, worker_id=None, actor=None):
        """Append one record to the tenant's audit stream.

        The ``sequence`` is assigned under the store lock, so concurrent
        appends stay unique and follow commit order, and it continues from
        the persisted stream, so a restart keeps increasing.  Only
        identifiers and the actor are stored — never params, results or
        error text; identifiers that do not apply are ``None``.
        """
        with self._lock:
            path = self.audit_path(tenant)
            items = (read_json(path, None) or {}).get("items") or []
            record = {
                "sequence": (items[-1]["sequence"] + 1) if items else 1,
                "at": at if at is not None else self.now_iso(),
                "tenant": tenant.strip(),
                "action": action,
                "run_id": run_id,
                "step_id": step_id,
                "workflow_id": workflow_id,
                "schedule_id": schedule_id,
                "worker_id": worker_id,
                "actor": actor,
            }
            items.append(record)
            atomic_write_json(path, {"items": items})
            return dict(record)

    def load_audit(self, tenant):
        """Return the tenant's audit records in sequence order (read-only)."""
        return list((read_json(self.audit_path(tenant), None) or {}).get("items") or [])

    # -- runs ----------------------------------------------------------
    def save_run(self, run):
        atomic_write_json(self.run_path(run["tenant"], run["run_id"]), run)
        return run

    def load_run(self, tenant, run_id):
        run = read_json(self.run_path(tenant, run_id), None)
        if run is None:
            raise WorkflowError("unknown run: %s" % run_id, "unknown_run")
        return normalize_run(run)

    def run_exists(self, run_id):
        """Return the tenant owning ``run_id``, or ``None``."""
        for tenant in sorted(os.listdir(self.root)):
            if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(self.root, tenant, "runs", "%s.json" % run_id)):
                return tenant
        return None

    def load_all_runs(self, tenant):
        """Return every run of the tenant as a list sorted by ``run_id``."""
        runs_dir = os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "runs")
        items = []
        for name in sorted(os.listdir(runs_dir)) if os.path.isdir(runs_dir) else []:
            run = read_json(os.path.join(runs_dir, name), None) if name.endswith(".json") else None
            if run is not None:
                items.append(normalize_run(run))
        items.sort(key=lambda r: r.get("run_id", ""))
        return items

    def list_runs(self, tenant, status=None, limit=50, after=None):
        runs_dir = os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "runs")
        items = []
        for name in sorted(os.listdir(runs_dir)) if os.path.isdir(runs_dir) else []:
            run = read_json(os.path.join(runs_dir, name), None) if name.endswith(".json") else None
            if run is not None:
                items.append(normalize_run(run))
        items.sort(key=lambda r: (r.get("created_at", ""), r.get("run_id", "")))
        if status:
            items = [r for r in items if r.get("status") == status]
        if after:
            position = [i for i, r in enumerate(items) if r.get("run_id") == after]
            items = items[position[0] + 1:] if position else []
        limit = max(1, int(limit))
        page = items[:limit]
        return page, (page[-1]["run_id"] if len(items) > limit else None)


def normalize_run(run):
    """Backfill fields missing from documents written by older versions.

    Steps without ``kind`` predate approval nodes and are ordinary tasks.
    Runs without ``max_parallelism`` predate per-run concurrency quotas and
    have no limit (``None``).  Runs without ``idempotency_key`` predate
    tenant-scoped idempotency keys and never participate in dedup (``None``).
    Runs without ``not_before`` predate delayed start and begin immediately
    (``None``).  Runs without ``schedule_id``/``scheduled_at`` predate
    periodic scheduling and were created manually (``None``).  Steps without
    ``next_attempt_at`` predate retry backoff and are immediately claimable
    (``None``).  Runs without a frozen ``plan`` predate per-run DAG snapshots
    and reconstruct theirs from the node definitions and ``step_order`` saved
    in the run document itself, so replay never has to read the workflow
    registry (which a later same-name submission may have overwritten).
    Steps without ``trigger_rule`` predate trigger rules and unlock only
    when every dependency succeeds (``all_success``); the same default is
    backfilled into frozen plan snapshots written before the field existed.
    Mutates and returns ``run``.
    """
    run.setdefault("max_parallelism", None)
    run.setdefault("idempotency_key", None)
    run.setdefault("not_before", None)
    run.setdefault("schedule_id", None)
    run.setdefault("scheduled_at", None)
    for step in run.get("steps", {}).values():
        step.setdefault("kind", KIND_TASK)
        step.setdefault("trigger_rule", TRIGGER_ALL_SUCCESS)
        step.setdefault("approval", None)
        step.setdefault("next_attempt_at", None)
    plan = run.get("plan")
    if plan:
        for planned in plan.get("steps") or []:
            planned.setdefault("trigger_rule", TRIGGER_ALL_SUCCESS)
    else:
        run["plan"] = plan_from_run(run)
    return run


def plan_from_run(run):
    """Reconstruct a normalized plan from the definitions frozen in a run.

    The run document keeps each node's ``kind``, ``depends_on`` and
    ``max_attempts`` together with ``step_order``; those are exactly the
    fields a plan needs, so documents written before plans were snapshotted
    remain replayable even after the workflow of the same id is overwritten
    or deleted.
    """
    steps = run.get("steps") or {}
    order = [sid for sid in (run.get("step_order") or sorted(steps)) if sid in steps]
    ordered = [
        {
            "id": steps[sid]["id"],
            "depends_on": list(steps[sid].get("depends_on") or []),
            "max_attempts": steps[sid]["max_attempts"],
            "kind": steps[sid].get("kind", KIND_TASK),
            "trigger_rule": steps[sid].get("trigger_rule", TRIGGER_ALL_SUCCESS),
        }
        for sid in order
    ]
    return {
        "workflow_id": run.get("workflow_id"),
        "steps": ordered,
        "order": [step["id"] for step in ordered],
    }


def run_plan(run):
    """Return the normalized DAG plan frozen into ``run`` at creation.

    Newer documents carry an explicit snapshot under ``plan``; older ones
    reconstruct it via :func:`plan_from_run` from the run's own nodes and
    ordering.  The result is a fresh copy, so callers can never mutate the
    snapshot stored in the run document.
    """
    snapshot = run.get("plan")
    if not snapshot or not snapshot.get("steps"):
        snapshot = plan_from_run(run)
    return {
        "workflow_id": snapshot.get("workflow_id", run.get("workflow_id")),
        "steps": [dict(step) for step in snapshot.get("steps", [])],
        "order": list(snapshot.get("order", [])),
    }


def new_run(tenant, workflow_id, run_id, params, plan, now_iso, max_parallelism=None,
            idempotency_key=None, not_before=None, schedule_id=None, scheduled_at=None):
    """Build a fresh run document from a validated plan."""
    steps = {
        step["id"]: {
            "id": step["id"],
            "kind": step.get("kind", KIND_TASK),
            "trigger_rule": step.get("trigger_rule", TRIGGER_ALL_SUCCESS),
            "depends_on": list(step["depends_on"]),
            "max_attempts": step["max_attempts"],
            "status": STEP_PENDING,
            "attempt": 0,
            "worker_id": None,
            "lease_deadline": None,
            "next_attempt_at": None,
            "ready_at": None,
            "started_at": None,
            "finished_at": None,
            "result": None,
            "error": None,
            "approval": None,
        }
        for step in plan["steps"]

43	        if length <= 0:
44	            return {}
45	        if length > MAX_BODY:
46	            raise WorkflowError("request body too large", "body_too_large")

3	Every command prints a single line of JSON to stdout.  Failures print a

"""Command line interface: ``python3 -m flowd [--data-dir DIR] <command>``.

Every command prints a single line of JSON to stdout.  Failures print a
single line of JSON to stderr and exit with a non-zero status.
"""

import argparse
import json
import sys

from .http_app import _run_view, create_server
from .model import WorkflowError
from .scheduler import Scheduler
from .store import WorkflowStore

DEFAULT_DATA_DIR = "./flowd_data"


def emit(payload):
    """Print one line of JSON to stdout."""
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=True, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    sys.stdout.flush()


def fail(message):
    """Print one line of JSON to stderr and return a non-zero exit code."""
    sys.stderr.write(json.dumps({"error": message}, ensure_ascii=True, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    sys.stderr.flush()
    return 1


def _step_args(parser, claim=False):
    """Shared arguments for the claim/complete/fail subcommands."""
    parser.add_argument("--run-id", required=True, dest="run_id")
    parser.add_argument("--tenant", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--worker", required=True)
    if claim:
        parser.add_argument("--lease-seconds", type=float, default=30.0, dest="lease_seconds")
    else:
        parser.add_argument("--step", required=True)
    return parser


def build_parser():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="flowd",
                                     description="distributed workflow orchestration backend")
    parser.add_argument("--data-dir", default=DEFAULT_DATA_DIR,
                        help="storage root (default: %(default)s)")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    serve = sub.add_parser("serve", help="run the HTTP API")
    serve.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
    serve.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8080)

    submit = sub.add_parser("submit", help="validate and store a workflow DAG")
    submit.add_argument("--tenant", required=True)
    submit.add_argument("--workflow", required=True)
    submit.add_argument("--file", required=True, help="JSON file holding a list of steps")

    status = sub.add_parser("status", help="show one run")
    status.add_argument("--run-id", required=True, dest="run_id")
    status.add_argument("--tenant", required=True)

    _step_args(sub.add_parser("claim", help="claim the next ready step"), claim=True)
    complete = _step_args(sub.add_parser("complete", help="complete a claimed step"))
    complete.add_argument("--result", help="optional JSON result")
    failure = _step_args(sub.add_parser("fail", help="fail a step (retry or exhaust attempts)"))
    failure.add_argument("--error", default="step failed")

    listing = sub.add_parser("list", help="list runs of a tenant")
    listing.add_argument("--tenant", required=True)
    listing.add_argument("--status")
    listing.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=50)
    return parser


def _load_steps(path):
    """Read a steps file: a JSON list, or an object with a ``steps`` list."""
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            payload = json.load(handle)
    except OSError as exc:
        raise WorkflowError("cannot read steps file: %s" % exc, "bad_file")
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise WorkflowError("steps file is not valid JSON: %s" % exc, "bad_json")
    if isinstance(payload, dict):
        payload = payload.get("steps")
    if not isinstance(payload, list):
        raise WorkflowError("steps file must contain a JSON list of steps", "bad_file")
    return payload


def _serve(store, scheduler, args):
    server = create_server(store, args.host, args.port, scheduler)
    emit({"ok": True, "host": args.host, "port": int(args.port), "data_dir": store.root})
    try:
        server.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        server.server_close()
    return 0


def main(argv=None):
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    try:
        store = WorkflowStore(args.data_dir)
        scheduler = Scheduler(store)
        if args.command == "serve":
            return _serve(store, scheduler, args)
        if args.command == "submit":
            plan = scheduler.submit(args.tenant, args.workflow, _load_steps(args.file))
            emit({"tenant": args.tenant, "workflow_id": plan["workflow_id"], "order": plan["order"]})
            return 0
        if args.command == "status":
            emit(_run_view(scheduler.get_run(args.tenant, args.run_id)))
            return 0
        if args.command == "claim":
            step = scheduler.claim(args.tenant, args.run_id, args.worker, args.lease_seconds)
            emit({"run_id": args.run_id, "step": step and {"id": step["id"],
                                                           "status": step["status"],
                                                           "attempt": step["attempt"]}})
            return 0
        if args.command == "complete":
            run = scheduler.complete(args.tenant, args.run_id, args.step, args.worker,
                                     json.loads(args.result) if args.result else None)
            emit({"run_id": run["run_id"], "status": run["status"]})
            return 0
        if args.command == "fail":
            run = scheduler.fail(args.tenant, args.run_id, args.step, args.worker, args.error)
            step = run["steps"][args.step]
            emit({"run_id": run["run_id"], "status": run["status"],
                  "step": {"id": args.step, "status": step["status"], "attempt": step["attempt"],
                           "next_attempt_at": step["next_attempt_at"]}})
            return 0
        if args.command == "list":
            items, next_after = scheduler.list_runs(args.tenant, args.status, args.limit)
            emit({"tenant": args.tenant, "next_after": next_after,
                  "items": [{"run_id": r["run_id"], "status": r["status"]} for r in items]})
            return 0
        return fail("unknown command: %s" % args.command)
    except WorkflowError as exc:
        return fail(exc.message)
    except ValueError as exc:
        return fail("invalid JSON argument: %s" % exc)
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        return fail("internal error: %s" % exc)


if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover
    sys.exit(main())

"""Tests for DAG validation (flowd.model)."""

import unittest

from flowd.model import DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS, WorkflowError, plan_workflow, topo_order


def steps(*specs):
    return [{"id": sid, "depends_on": list(deps)} for sid, deps in specs]


class ValidationTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_plan_is_topologically_sorted(self):
        plan = plan_workflow("etl", steps(("c", ["b"]), ("a", []), ("b", ["a"])))
        self.assertEqual(plan["order"], ["a", "b", "c"])
        self.assertEqual([s["id"] for s in plan["steps"]], ["a", "b", "c"])
        self.assertEqual(plan["workflow_id"], "etl")

    def test_topo_order_is_deterministic_for_independent_steps(self):
        self.assertEqual(topo_order(steps(("z", []), ("a", []), ("m", []))), ["a", "m", "z"])

    def test_default_max_attempts(self):
        self.assertEqual(plan_workflow("w", steps(("a", [])))["steps"][0]["max_attempts"],
                         DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS)

    def test_duplicate_id_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(WorkflowError) as ctx:
            plan_workflow("w", steps(("a", []), ("a", [])))
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "duplicate_step")

    def test_unknown_dependency_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(WorkflowError) as ctx:
            plan_workflow("w", steps(("a", ["ghost"])))
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "unknown_dependency")
        self.assertIn("ghost", ctx.exception.message)

    def test_self_dependency_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(WorkflowError) as ctx:
            plan_workflow("w", steps(("a", ["a"])))
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "self_dependency")

    def test_cycle_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(WorkflowError) as ctx:
            plan_workflow("w", steps(("a", ["c"]), ("b", ["a"]), ("c", ["b"])))
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "cycle")
        self.assertEqual(sorted(ctx.exception.message.split(": ")[1].split(", ")), ["a", "b", "c"])

    def test_longer_cycle_is_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(WorkflowError) as ctx:
            plan_workflow("w", steps(("a", []), ("b", ["a", "c"]), ("c", ["b"])))
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "cycle")

    def test_empty_id_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(WorkflowError) as ctx:
            plan_workflow("w", [{"id": "   ", "depends_on": []}])
        self.assertIn("empty id", ctx.exception.message)
        with self.assertRaises(WorkflowError):
            plan_workflow("w", [{"depends_on": []}])

    def test_bad_max_attempts_rejected(self):
        for bad in (0, -3, "three", 2.5, True):
            with self.assertRaises(WorkflowError) as ctx:
                plan_workflow("w", [{"id": "a", "max_attempts": bad}])
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "bad_max_attempts", "value %r" % (bad,))

    def test_duplicate_dependency_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(WorkflowError):
            plan_workflow("w", steps(("a", []), ("b", ["a", "a"])))

    def test_bad_workflow_id_and_empty_steps_rejected(self):
        for bad_id in ("", "   ", None, 7):
            with self.assertRaises(WorkflowError):
                plan_workflow(bad_id, steps(("a", [])))
        with self.assertRaises(WorkflowError):
            plan_workflow("w", [])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""End-to-end tests for the stdlib HTTP API."""

import json
import shutil
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

from flowd.http_app import create_server
from flowd.store import WorkflowStore

LINEAR = [
    {"id": "step1", "depends_on": []},
    {"id": "step2", "depends_on": ["step1"]},
    {"id": "step3", "depends_on": ["step2"]},
]


class HttpTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.root = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="flowd-http-")
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.root, True)
        self.server = create_server(WorkflowStore(self.root), "127.0.0.1", 0)
        self.port = self.server.server_address[1]
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        self.addCleanup(self.server.server_close)
        self.addCleanup(self.server.shutdown)

    def call(self, method, path, body=None, raw_body=None):
        """Return (status, parsed json or None); never raises on HTTP errors."""
        data = raw_body
        if body is not None:
            data = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
        request = urllib.request.Request("http://127.0.0.1:%d%s" % (self.port, path),
                                        data=data, method=method)
        if data is not None:
            request.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=10) as response:
                payload = response.read()
                return response.status, (json.loads(payload) if payload else None)
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            payload = exc.read()
            return exc.code, (json.loads(payload) if payload else None)

    def submit_workflow(self, tenant="acme", workflow_id="etl", steps=None):
        status, body = self.call("POST", "/v1/workflows",
                                 {"tenant": tenant, "workflow_id": workflow_id,
                                  "steps": LINEAR if steps is None else steps})
        self.assertEqual(status, 201, body)
        return body

    def start_run(self, tenant="acme", workflow_id="etl", run_id=None):
        payload = {"tenant": tenant, "workflow_id": workflow_id}
        if run_id:
            payload["run_id"] = run_id
        status, body = self.call("POST", "/v1/runs", payload)
        self.assertEqual(status, 201, body)
        return body

    def claim(self, run_id="r1", tenant="acme", worker="w1", lease=60):
        return self.call("POST", "/v1/runs/%s/claim" % run_id,
                         {"tenant": tenant, "worker_id": worker, "lease_seconds": lease})

    def complete(self, step_id, run_id="r1", tenant="acme", worker="w1"):
        return self.call("POST", "/v1/runs/%s/complete" % run_id,
                         {"tenant": tenant, "step_id": step_id, "worker_id": worker})

    def drive(self, run_id="r1"):
        """Claim/complete the whole linear DAG over HTTP."""
        body = None
        for expected in ("step1", "step2", "step3"):
            status, body = self.claim(run_id)
            self.assertEqual(status, 200, body)
            self.assertEqual(body["step"]["id"], expected)
            status, body = self.complete(expected, run_id)
            self.assertEqual(status, 200, body)
        return body

    def test_healthz(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.call("GET", "/healthz"), (200, {"ok": True}))

    def test_workflow_submit_and_validation_error(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.submit_workflow()["order"], ["step1", "step2", "step3"])
        status, body = self.call("POST", "/v1/workflows",
                                 {"tenant": "acme", "workflow_id": "bad",
                                  "steps": [{"id": "a", "depends_on": ["ghost"]}]})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)
        self.assertIn("ghost", body["error"])

    def test_malformed_json_returns_400(self):
        status, body = self.call("POST", "/v1/workflows", raw_body=b"{not json")
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)
        self.assertIn("error", body)

    def test_run_lifecycle_over_http(self):
        self.submit_workflow()
        run = self.start_run(run_id="r1")
        self.assertEqual(run["status"], "pending")
        self.assertEqual([s["status"] for s in run["steps"]], ["ready", "pending", "pending"])
        self.assertEqual(self.drive()["status"], "succeeded")
        status, body = self.call("GET", "/v1/runs/r1?tenant=acme")
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["status"], "succeeded")
        self.assertEqual([s["status"] for s in body["steps"]], ["succeeded"] * 3)

    def test_claim_returns_204_when_nothing_ready(self):
        self.submit_workflow()
        self.start_run(run_id="r1")
        self.drive()
        self.assertEqual(self.claim(), (204, None))

    def test_fail_retries_then_exhausts(self):
        self.submit_workflow(workflow_id="flaky",
                             steps=[{"id": "s", "depends_on": [], "max_attempts": 2}])
        self.start_run(workflow_id="flaky", run_id="r2")
        self.claim("r2")
        status, body = self.call("POST", "/v1/runs/r2/fail",
                                 {"tenant": "acme", "step_id": "s", "worker_id": "w1",
                                  "error": "boom"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        step = body["steps"][0]
        self.assertEqual((step["status"], step["attempt"]), ("ready", 1))
        self.assertIsNotNone(step["next_attempt_at"])
        # The backoff (1s by default) has not elapsed: no lease, no changes.
        before = self.call("GET", "/v1/runs/r2?tenant=acme")[1]
        self.assertEqual(self.claim("r2"), (204, None))
        after = self.call("GET", "/v1/runs/r2?tenant=acme")[1]
        self.assertEqual(after["updated_at"], before["updated_at"])
        self.assertEqual(after["history_length"], before["history_length"])
        time.sleep(1.1)  # wait out the backoff
        status, body = self.claim("r2")
        self.assertEqual(status, 200, body)
        self.assertIsNone(body["step"]["next_attempt_at"])
        status, body = self.call("POST", "/v1/runs/r2/fail",
                                 {"tenant": "acme", "step_id": "s", "worker_id": "w1",
                                  "error": "boom again"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["status"], "failed")
        self.assertEqual(body["steps"][0]["status"], "failed")

    def test_complete_without_lease_is_409(self):

"""Tests for the run state machine, leases, retries, history and replay."""

import os
import shutil
import tempfile
import unittest

from flowd.model import WorkflowError
from flowd.scheduler import ConflictError, LeaseError, Scheduler, backoff_seconds
from flowd.store import WorkflowStore

LINEAR = [
    {"id": "step1", "depends_on": []},
    {"id": "step2", "depends_on": ["step1"]},
    {"id": "step3", "depends_on": ["step2"]},
]


class FakeClock:
    """Injectible deterministic clock; sleeping advances virtual time."""

    def __init__(self, start=1_700_000_000.0):
        self.value = float(start)

    def __call__(self):
        return self.value

    def advance(self, seconds):
        self.value += float(seconds)
        return self.value

    def sleep(self, seconds):
        self.advance(seconds)


class SchedulerTestBase(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.root = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="flowd-test-")
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.root, True)
        self.clock = FakeClock()
        self.store = WorkflowStore(self.root, clock=self.clock)
        self.scheduler = Scheduler(self.store, clock=self.clock, backoff_base=1.0)

    def workflow(self, workflow_id="etl", steps=None):
        return self.scheduler.submit("acme", workflow_id, steps or LINEAR)

    def claim(self, run_id, worker="w1", lease=30, tenant="acme"):
        return self.scheduler.claim(tenant, run_id, worker, lease)

    def complete(self, run_id, step_id, worker="w1", result=None, tenant="acme"):
        return self.scheduler.complete(tenant, run_id, step_id, worker, result)

    def finish_next(self, run_id, worker="w1"):
        """Claim and complete the next ready step."""
        step = self.claim(run_id, worker)
        return step, self.complete(run_id, step["id"], worker)


class StateMachineTest(SchedulerTestBase):
    def test_step_becomes_ready_only_after_dependencies_succeed(self):
        self.workflow()
        run = self.scheduler.start_run("acme", "etl")
        self.assertEqual(run["status"], "pending")
        self.assertEqual([s["status"] for s in run["steps"].values()],
                         ["ready", "pending", "pending"])

        self.assertEqual(self.claim(run["run_id"])["id"], "step1")
        self.assertIsNone(self.claim(run["run_id"]))
        run = self.complete(run["run_id"], "step1", result={"rows": 3})
        self.assertEqual(run["status"], "running")
        self.assertEqual(run["steps"]["step2"]["status"], "ready")
        self.assertEqual(run["steps"]["step3"]["status"], "pending")

        for sid in ("step2", "step3"):
            _, run = self.finish_next(run["run_id"])
            self.assertEqual(run["steps"][sid]["status"], "succeeded")
        self.assertEqual(run["status"], "succeeded")
        self.assertTrue(all(s["status"] == "succeeded" for s in run["steps"].values()))

    def test_claim_orders_ready_steps_deterministically(self):
        self.workflow("fan", [{"id": "b", "depends_on": []}, {"id": "a", "depends_on": []}])
        run = self.scheduler.start_run("acme", "fan")
        self.assertEqual(self.claim(run["run_id"])["id"], "a")
        self.assertEqual(self.claim(run["run_id"])["id"], "b")
        self.assertIsNone(self.claim(run["run_id"]))
